title: movie review database
subtitle: Oracle PL/SQL relational system
overview: A normalised relational database for movies, users, reviews, and genres — with the business logic living in the database itself, not an app layer.
credit: Team project at TIET (DBMS / UCS310), with 2 collaborators.
body: Movie recommendations tend to live in scattered, inconsistent places — word of mouth, isolated ratings, no real structure behind any of it. This project builds a centralised, normalised relational database that stores movies, users, reviews, and genres with real integrity guarantees, and puts the business logic inside the database itself rather than in an app layer.

The design started as an ER diagram and mapped down to five tables — users, movies, reviews, genres, and a movie_genres junction table resolving the many-to-many between movies and genres. Users and movies each relate to reviews one-to-many; movies and genres relate many-to-many. Everything is normalised to third normal form, justified table by table in the write-up.

The actual engineering is in the PL/SQL: a movie_crud stored procedure handles add/edit/remove with proper exception handling via RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR; an add_review procedure inserts a review and atomically bumps the user's score in the same block, so a failure rolls back both instead of leaving things half-written. Cursor procedures handle reporting — view_all_reviews and view_all_movie_reviews use implicit cursors, and display_movie_genres uses nested cursors to print each movie alongside its genres. Two views, top_movies and top_users, wrap the common reporting queries (joins plus group-by) into reusable interfaces.

The write-up explicitly maps the design onto ACID: atomicity through the single-block review-and-score update, consistency through foreign key and not-null constraints, isolation through Oracle's multi-version read consistency, and durability through commit and redo logs — along with how commit, rollback, and savepoint define the transaction boundaries. It's a genuine backend database project, not just a schema diagram.
Complete and submitted. Extensible toward recommendation or sentiment features, or a front end.
